question: Methotrexate can be used to treat ectopic pregnancy in a haemodynamically unstable patient if the ectopic mass is small (<3.5 cm) and no free fluid is seen on ultrasound.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is FALSE. Haemodynamic instability is an absolute contraindication to methotrexate regardless of sac size or ultrasound findings. Emergency surgical management (laparoscopic salpingectomy) is required. Methotrexate is only for stable, unruptured ectopic pregnancies meeting strict criteria.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Haemodynamic instability is an ABSOLUTE contraindication to methotrexate. Any sign of haemodynamic compromise (tachycardia, hypotension, collapse) mandates emergency surgery — salpingectomy or salpingostomy. Small size criteria apply only when the patient is haemodynamically stable.
